summary: Sumburgh Airport is the main gateway to the Shetland Islands, located at the southern tip of the Shetland Mainland in Scotland. The airport plays a dual role as both a vital regional transport hub and a major base for North Sea oil and gas industry helicopter operations. Its dramatic clifftop setting near Sumburgh Head and the prehistoric Jarlshof archaeological site makes it one of the most scenically situated airports in the United Kingdom.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly from Sumburgh Airport?
A: Loganair is the primary scheduled carrier, operating direct flights to Aberdeen, Edinburgh, and Glasgow, connecting Shetland to mainland Scotland.

Q: How far is Sumburgh Airport from Lerwick?
A: The airport is approximately 25 miles (40 km) south of Lerwick, with the drive taking around 45 minutes via the A970 road.

Q: Does Sumburgh handle helicopter flights to oil rigs?
A: Yes, the airport is a major hub for offshore helicopter operations serving North Sea oil and gas platforms, operated by companies such as Bristow and CHC Helicopter.

Q: Can I see puffins near the airport?
A: Yes, Sumburgh Head, just a short drive from the airport, is home to a large seabird colony featuring puffins during the summer breeding season.
transport_tips: Renting a car is highly recommended as public transport options are limited, though taxi services and a seasonal bus (number 6) connect the airport to Lerwick. Pre-booking a taxi is advisable, especially for early morning or late evening flights, as availability can be limited. If traveling onward to other Shetland islands, ferries depart from Lerwick, so plan at least two hours between your flight arrival and ferry departure.
local_tip: If you have a long layover or a cancelled flight, take the short trip to Sumburgh Head lighthouse and nature reserve just minutes from the terminal. The clifftop walk offers dramatic views, and the on-site café is a favorite among pilots and crew looking to pass the time.
